Berchtoldstag Hazelnut Torte

Served at: Berchtoldstag

Serves 8-10Prep 40 minCook 50 min

The Hazelnut Torte, or Haselnusstorte, is a beloved Swiss pastry, perfect for celebrating Berchtoldstag on January 2nd. This holiday, primarily observed in Switzerland, is a time for family gatherings and enjoying rich, comforting treats. This torte, with its buttery crust and sweet, nutty filling, embodies the warmth and tradition of the festive season.

Ingredients

  • For the Dough:
  • 2 cups (250 g) all-purpose flour
  • 1/3 cup + 1 tablespoon (80 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (115 g) unsalted butter, cold and cubed
  • 1 large egg
  • Pinch of salt
  • Zest of 1/2 lemon
  • For the Filling:
  • 2 cups (200 g) ground hazelnuts
  • 3/4 cup (150 g) granulated sugar
  • 1/2 cup (120 ml) heavy cream
  • 2 tablespoons honey or maple syrup
  • 1 large egg yolk
  • 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
  • 1/2 teaspoon ground cinnamon
  • For Assembly:
  • 1 large egg, beaten (for egg wash)
  • Powdered sugar, for dusting (optional)

Method

  1. To make the dough: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, salt, and lemon zest. Add the cold, cubed butter and cut it into the flour mixture using a pastry blender or your fingertips until it resembles coarse crumbs.
  2. Add the egg and mix until the dough just comes together. Do not overmix. Form the dough into a disc, wrap it in plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes.
  3. To make the filling: In a medium bowl, combine the ground hazelnuts, sugar, heavy cream, honey (or maple syrup), egg yolk, vanilla extract, and cinnamon. Mix well until thoroughly combined.
  4. Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C). Grease and lightly flour a 9-inch (23 cm) springform pan.
  5. Divide the chilled dough into two portions: one larger (about 2/3 of the dough) for the base and sides, and one smaller (about 1/3) for the top crust.
  6. On a lightly floured surface, roll out the larger dough portion into a circle large enough to cover the bottom and extend up the sides of the prepared springform pan. Carefully transfer the dough to the pan, pressing it gently into the bottom and up the sides.
  7. Spread the hazelnut filling evenly over the dough in the pan.
  8. Roll out the smaller dough portion into a circle slightly larger than the top of the pan. Carefully place it over the filling.
  9. Trim any excess dough from the edges, leaving a small overhang. Crimp the edges of the top and bottom crusts together to seal the torte. You can use a fork to create a decorative edge.
  10. Brush the top of the torte with the beaten egg wash. Using a fork, prick the top crust several times to allow steam to escape during baking.
  11. Bake for 45-55 minutes, or until the crust is golden brown and the filling is set. If the crust starts to brown too quickly, you can loosely cover it with aluminum foil.
  12. Remove the torte from the oven and let it cool completely on a wire rack before removing the springform pan. This is crucial for the torte to set properly.
  13. Once cooled, you may dust the top with powdered sugar before slicing and serving.

Tips

  • For best flavor and texture, allow the torte to cool completely, ideally overnight, before serving. This allows the flavors to meld beautifully.
  • You can substitute walnuts or almonds for hazelnuts, though it will change the traditional flavor profile.
  • Store the torte at room temperature, covered, for up to 3-4 days, or refrigerate for longer freshness.
